content.text: I assume this is an issue w/ earlier versions of Fedora as well, since this method hasn't really changed (although the stacktrace might have as a result of springification).
Every time we have to fix Server related code I despair at the difficulty of adding unit test coverage. Anyway, I have a test case almost ready, so I'll get this committed in the next day or so.

Whoops, I should've read the comments first. I didn't realize you had a test case in the works Eddie. I just merged it without one, but of course, having a test case even for simple stuff like this is preferable.
Thanks Eddie – I couldn't figure out how to test the initModule() method, I'm glad you're on it.
Not sure how many versions back this issue affects, but tagging 3.5 and 3.6 for the moment
When the tomcat user (etc) does not have permission to create the server/management/uploads directory, you get a NPE with an obscure error message (stacktrace below).

. The `mkdirs` command may return false when it is unable to create the directory tree (note, it also returns false if the directory already exists). I assume it should throw an exception if the upload directory doesn't exist and can't be created?
Caused by: java.lang.RuntimeException: Fatal error while starting server

Caused by: org.springframework.beans.factory.BeanCreationException: Error creating bean with name 'org.fcrepo.server.management.Management': Invocation of init method failed; nested exception is org.fcrepo.server.errors.ModuleInitializationException: Error while initializing temporary storage area: java.lang.NullPointerException: null
Caused by: org.fcrepo.server.errors.ModuleInitializationException: Error while initializing temporary storage area: java.lang.NullPointerException: null

When the tomcat user (etc) does not have permission to create the server/management/uploads directory, you get a NPE with an obscure error message (stacktrace below).

I tracked the error to https://github.com/fcrepo/fcrepo/blob/master/fcrepo-server/src/main/java/org/fcrepo/server/management/ManagementModule.java#L107. The `mkdirs` command may return false when it is unable to create the directory tree (note, it also returns false if the directory already exists). I assume it should throw an exception if the upload directory doesn't exist and can't be created?
